'''Peter M. Bentler''' is an American psychologist, statistician, and distinguished professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].

In [[multivariate analysis]] and [[psychometrics]], Bentler is the developer of the [[structural equation modeling]] software EQS.<ref>[http://www.mvsoft.com/eqsintro.htm EQS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502181549/http://www.mvsoft.com/eqsintro.htm |date=2017-05-02 }}.</ref> Bentler received a doctorate in clinical psychology from [[Stanford University]] in 1964.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.psych.ucla.edu/sites/default/files/documents/publications/Bentler%20CV%20by%20Topics%20May%202018.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2020-08-22 |archive-date=2021-07-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729221755/https://www.psych.ucla.edu/sites/default/files/documents/publications/Bentler%20CV%20by%20Topics%20May%202018.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> His publications have over 300,000 citations {{as of|2023|lc=y}}.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=esb4VbgAAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar entry for Peter M. Bentler].</ref> In 2014, he was awarded the Psychometric Society Career Award.<ref>[https://www.psychometricsociety.org/content/peter-bentler-wins-2014-psychometric-society-career-award Psychometric Society]</ref> In 2015, he was elected [[List of Fellows of the American Statistical Association|Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |title=ASA Fellows Page |access-date=2015-09-01 |archive-date=2016-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
